Pradeep Kori @ Bholu .... Petitioner
 Mr. A.K. Raut, Advocate
 -versus-
 State of Odisha ....

Opposite Party
 Mr. P.K. Maharaj, Asc
 Mr. P.K. Sahoo, Advocate
 (Informant)
 Coram: Justice V. Narasingh
 Order
07.10.2024 Order No.
02. 1.
Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner, learned counsel for the State and learned counsel for the Informant.

2. The Petitioner is an accused in connection with C.T. Case No.1292 of 2024, pending on the file of learned S.D.J.M., Jharsuguda arising out of Banharpali P.S. Case No.100 of 2024 for commission of the alleged offence under Section 417/493/494/495/506 of IPC.
3. Learned counsel, on instruction, submits that except the present BLAPL, no other bail application of the Petitioner relating to the aforementioned P.S. case is pending in any other Court.

4. Being aggrieved by the rejection of his application for bail U/s.483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) by the learned ADJ-cum- P.O. Special Court POCSO, Jharsuguda by order dated 04.07.2024 in the aforementioned case, the present BLAPL has been filed.

5. It is submitted by the learned counsel that the Petitioner is in custody since 17.06.2024 and as charge sheet in the case at hand has been filed on 15.08.2024, the Petitioner may be released on bail.
6. Learned counsel for the State as well as learned counsel for the Informant oppose the prayer for bail.

sentences.text: It is submitted by the learned counsel for the Informant that apart from the case at hand the Petitioner is cited as an accused in Katni P.S. Case No.208 dated 11.05.2024 under Section 376(2)(n) of IPC.
Hence, keeping in view his criminal proclivity, the Petitioner ought not to be released on bail.
8. The final form of Katni P.S. Case No.208 dated 11.05.2024 in which the petitioner has been cited as an accused is taken on record.
9. This Court perused the 164 Cr.P.C. Statement of the victim.
10. Considering the same and taking into account the submission of final form, this Court directs the Petitioner to be released on bail on such terms to be fixed by the learned Court in seisin.

11. Keeping in view the criminal antecedent of the Petitioner, additionally, it is directed that Petitioner shall appear before the jurisdictional police station twice every week on such date and time to be fixed by the learned Court in seisin till conclusion of trial.
Certification of such appearance shall be submitted to the Court in seisin.
12. It is directed that the Petitioner shall not in any way try to intimidate the victim and her family.
13. It shall be open to the victim/Prosecution to seek variance of this order, in the event there is any threat perception.
14. Accordingly, the BLAPL stands disposed of.
15. Urgent certified copy of this order be granted as per rules.
(V. NARASINGH) Judge Ayesha Designation: Junior Stenographer
